name: What Is a Fault Tree
title: What Is a Fault Tree
description: A fault tree is a top-down diagram: the undesired top event at the top, connected through AND/OR gates to intermediate events, down to basic events (component failures, human errors). It answers 'how could this happen?'
how_it_works: Start from the feared event, ask 'how could this occur' repeatedly, and connect causes with logic gates. The tree is read top-down for causation, bottom-up for prevention.
key_points: Top-down for causation; bottom-up for prevention.
requirements: A defined top event (undesired); system decomposition to basic events; failure data or estimates for quantification.
standards: Fault tree analysis practice (IEC 61025); reliability engineering methods.
citations: IEC 61025 fault tree analysis standard.
NASA fault tree handbook with aerospace examples.

name: AND vs OR Gates
title: AND vs OR Gates
description: OR gates mean any input causes the output (redundancy defeated by single failures); AND gates mean all inputs must coincide (defense in depth). Gate choice is the logic of the analysis.
how_it_works: Use OR where any single cause suffices, AND where coincidence is required. Getting gates wrong inverts the risk picture - review gate logic carefully.
requirements: A defined top event (undesired); system decomposition to basic events; failure data or estimates for quantification.
standards: Fault tree analysis practice (IEC 61025); reliability engineering methods.
citations: IEC 61025 fault tree analysis standard.
NASA fault tree handbook with aerospace examples.

requirements: A defined top event (undesired); system decomposition to basic events; failure data or estimates for quantification.
standards: Fault tree analysis practice (IEC 61025); reliability engineering methods.

name: Minimal Cut Sets
title: Minimal Cut Sets
description: Minimal cut sets are the smallest combinations of basic events that cause the top event. Single-event cut sets are single points of failure - the tree's most important output.
how_it_works: Compute cut sets (software helps for large trees), highlight singletons as single points of failure, and prioritize fixes by cut set order and probability. Cut sets turn trees into action lists.
key_points: Smallest cause-combinations for the top event.
Trees become action lists via cut sets.
requirements: A defined top event (undesired); system decomposition to basic events; failure data or estimates for quantification.
standards: Fault tree analysis practice (IEC 61025); reliability engineering methods.
citations: IEC 61025 fault tree analysis standard.

name: Common Cause in Fault Trees
title: Common Cause in Fault Trees
description: Common-cause failures need explicit modeling: beta-factor or explicit shared events. Trees that ignore common cause underestimate risk systematically.
how_it_works: Add common-cause basic events or beta factors to redundant branches, justify the parameters, and check sensitivity. Redundancy without common-cause modeling is optimistic.
requirements: A defined top event (undesired); system decomposition to basic events; failure data or estimates for quantification.
standards: Fault tree analysis practice (IEC 61025); reliability engineering methods.
